title: The Return of the Scuderia
paragraphs: After narrowly missing out on the title in both 1998 and 1999, Ferrari entered the new millennium determined to end one of the longest championship droughts in Formula One history. Michael Schumacher, joined by Rubens Barrichello in his first season with the Scuderia, once again faced fierce competition from Mika Häkkinen and McLaren, setting the stage for another chapter in one of the sport's greatest rivalries.

Throughout the season, Schumacher and Häkkinen exchanged victories as neither team managed to establish complete control. Their battle produced some of Formula One's most memorable moments, none more famous than Schumacher's breathtaking overtake on Häkkinen at Spa-Francorchamps while lapping Ricardo Zonta, a move that has become one of the defining images of modern Formula One.

The championship remained finely balanced heading into the closing races, with momentum swinging between Ferrari and McLaren. Schumacher ultimately secured the Drivers' Championship at the penultimate round in Japan, while Ferrari claimed the Constructors' Championship for a second consecutive season after another year of relentless competition.

Schumacher's victory ended Ferrari's 21-year wait for a Drivers' World Championship, the team's first since Jody Scheckter in 1979. More importantly, it marked the beginning of one of the most successful dynasties in Formula One history, as Ferrari and Schumacher would go on to dominate the sport for the next five seasons.
